text: {"findings":[{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Unsourced late-delivery churn and cost figures","detail":"The 12% never-reorder rate and $48M annual cost are stated as fact with only a vague 'industry data' attribution and no citation. The problem sizing cannot be verified.","evidence_quote":"Industry data shows that 12% of customers never reorder after a late delivery, costing roughly $48M a year.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite the specific source or internal analysis for the 12% and $48M figures, or restate them as estimates with methodology."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing guardrails for credit/incentive behavior change","detail":"Issuing automatic credits changes cost and customer behavior, but the only guardrail is Cost Per Delivery. There are no guardrails for credit abuse or fraud, late-delivery rate or on-time performance, order volume or reorder rate, or support contacts.","evidence_quote":"Cost Per Delivery: stop if it rises by more than $0.15.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as credit redemption/abuse rate, on-time delivery rate, contribution margin per order, and customer support contact rate, each with thresholds."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days of effective observation and mismatched to the metric window","detail":"A 3-week run does not cover the 8-week success window, and the credit is applied to the next order, so effects on reorder behavior will not be observed within 3 weeks. Late orders are also only a subset of traffic, so a 0.15 CSAT MDE may be underpowered, and no sample size is given. Customer-level randomization may also leak through shared households or accounts.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by customer. Duration: 3 weeks. MDE: 0.15 CSAT points, power 80%.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Align the experiment duration with the 8-week target and reorder-based measurement. Provide a sample-size calculation based on the volume of late orders and justify the MDE against the +0.3 target."},{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Credit program lacks recorded review beyond informing Finance","detail":"Automatic monetary credits are a pay/promotional-spend change that requires formal sign-off. The proposal only says Finance was 'informed', which is not an approval or a recorded review. Legal/policy review of the credit terms is not recorded either.","evidence_quote":"Finance has been informed of the expected credit volume.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Record formal Finance approval of the credit budget and any required legal or policy review of the credit terms."},{"type":"NO_BASELINE_TARGET","title":"Credit value and cost threshold lack defined parameters","detail":"The credit is only described as 'fixed-value' with no amount, so cost impact and the $0.15 guardrail cannot be evaluated. The success metric is also limited to CSAT, with no baseline or target for the retention outcome the problem cites.","evidence_quote":"Automatically apply a fixed-value credit to the next order","citations":[],"recommendation":"Specify the credit amount and add a retention metric, such as repeat order rate within 30 days, with a baseline, target, and timeframe."}]}
